title: Packetized Observability Bridge for OTLP->Prometheus and KPI Normalization
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Background: We currently receive OTLP metrics and Prometheus-style scrape data in separate pipelines. Several consumers (dashboards, SLO compute jobs, and per-customer cost attribution) need a unified, normalized stream of inference KPIs (latency P50/P99, token counts, error categories, cold-start markers) with deterministic labels and exemplar linkage.

Goal: Implement a packetized, tenant-aware observability bridge that: (1) accepts OTLP/OTLP-HTTP and Prometheus remote_write payloads, (2) normalizes labels/value types to a canonical schema for inference KPIs, (3) emits both a Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoint (for compatibility) and a compact OTLP-forwarding path for downstream SLO and billing systems, and (4) supports adaptive sampling and exemplar-preserving downsampling to reduce cardinality while keeping signal for tail latency and error hotspots.

Scope: This ticket covers the bridge service prototype, mapping rules for key inference KPIs, an initial set of label normalization rules (tenant, model, deployment_variant, sequence_length_bucket), and integration tests plus a dashboard demonstrating parity with current ingestion. Separate follow-ups will handle autoscaling policies and multi-region routing.

Non-Goals: Full rollout to Dedicated clusters, long-term retention migration, and UI changes to Console (except a demo dashboard).

Performance Targets: ingest pipeline must sustain 50k metric points/sec per instance with median processing latency < 100ms and 99th < 500ms under steady-state load. Cardinality target: reduce combinatorial label explosion by >70% for typical production workloads via deterministic normalization and prefix canonicalization.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge can accept OTLP gRPC and OTLP-HTTP traffic and return 202 on valid payloads
Canonical label mapping applied for tenant, model, deployment_variant, and sequence_length_bucket
Prometheus remote_write payloads are accepted and converted to canonical OTLP metrics with exemplar preservation
Adaptive sampling reduces stored metric cardinality by >=70% on synthetic traffic with preserved P99 latency exemplars
Integration tests exercising a sample app show metric parity (within 2%) against current ingestion pipeline for P50/P95/P99 latency and token_count totals
End-to-end demo dashboard shows per-tenant latency heatmap and error-rate alerting working with bridge output
tasks: Design: finalize canonical schema and mapping doc
Implement receiver adapters for OTLP gRPC, OTLP-HTTP, and remote_write
Label normalizer: ruleset + whitelist/blacklist + prefix canonicalization
Exemplar linker: deterministic exemplar tags based on request-id hashing
Adaptive sampler: reservoir sampling + stride downsampler tuned for tail preservation
Forwarder: dual-path to Prometheus exporter and OTLP downstream export
Performance runbook and benchmark harness + resource sizing guidance
comments: 2026-02-11 - Nina Patel: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence. Agreed to favor deterministic label mapping over ad-hoc blacklisting to prevent drift.
2026-02-18 - Marco Liu: Prototype receiver implemented for OTLP-HTTP and validated with jaeger-opentelemetry-py sample app. Initial CPU profile attached to PR.

2026-02-26 - Sofia Ramirez (PM): Reviewed mapping doc. Requested sequence_length_bucket granularity change from [0-32,33-128,129+] to finer buckets [0-16,17-64,65-256,256+]. Marked customer_impact as high due to billing and SLO use cases.

2026-03-03 - Marco Liu: Added exemplar linker that tags metrics with deterministic request-hash; verified correlation across traces and metrics for test traffic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/842
2026-03-09 - Ops: Load test at 40k pts/sec per instance. Observed GC pauses causing 99th latency spikes; adjusted JVM flags and dropped median latency to 85ms. Follow-up to tune buffer sizing.
2026-03-12 - Nina Patel: Running integration tests with Prometheus remote_write fixtures. Found label collision for model aliases; implementing alias resolution table as part of normalizer.
notes: Trade-offs and decisions: chose packetized processing (fixed-size batches) to bound memory and provide backpressure instead of per-metric streaming which amplified cardinality spikes. Deterministic exemplar tagging chosen to make trace<->metric correlation reproducible for debugging. Risks: unforeseen label sources from customer-provided metadata may reintroduce cardinality—mitigation is alias/whitelist enforcement and a nightly denylist job. Next steps: complete remote_write adapter, finish integration tests, and run a 24h canary in staging with tenant sampling enabled.
